paper.title_en: Sensitivity to $Θ^+$ production in the $π^- p \to K^- X$ reaction at HIAF-HIRIBL
paper.abstract_en: Pion-induced searches for the $Θ^+$ can probe the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation region beyond the E19 energies. We present sensitivity projections for a missing-mass search for a narrow $Θ^+$ at 1.540 GeV/$c^2$ in $π^- p \to K^- X$ at the High Intensity heavy-ion Accelerator Facility and its HIgh-rigidity Radioactive Ion Beam Line. With the E19 resolutions, efficiency, and continuum, separate 10-day exposures at pion momenta of 2.01 and 2.586 GeV/$c$ give background-only median expected 90% CL upper limits of 0.0293 and 0.0356 $μ$b/sr, respectively, on the differential cross section averaged over $2^\circ$ to $15^\circ$ on the selected high-momentum branch; the higher momentum corresponds to the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation energy. Median local $5σ$ discovery thresholds are 0.0894 and 0.109 $μ$b/sr. Nonresonant nucleon-exchange models give width scales of 0.0039 to 0.079 MeV for $J^P=1/2^+$ and 0.045 to 1.47 MeV for $J^P=1/2^-$. All positive-parity variants would test the DIANA width scale of $0.34 \pm 0.10$ MeV; negative-parity sensitivity depends on the variant.
